insights.insight: The protocol has logged 12,411 cryptographically verified receipts spanning grocery, fuel, dining, warehouse, and SaaS — each one a confirmed transaction, not a behavioral inference. At $996K in verified GMV, the dataset is small but structurally distinct from any probabilistic targeting stack.

The network sits $3,996 from $1M in verified GMV, with the most recent single heartbeat adding $2,055 — meaning the crossing is within one or two data cycles. This is the first auditable commerce milestone of this kind for the protocol and marks a natural evaluation checkpoint for prospective data buyers.

insights.topic: Velocity deceleration with early stabilization signal
insights.insight: Week-over-week token velocity dropped from a peak of 1.241x on April 12 to a trough of 0.819x on April 17 morning — the sharpest single-cycle deceleration on record — before recovering modestly to 0.855x with acceleration now at 1.013x. The recovery is real but unconfirmed; one additional heartbeat of upward movement is required before treating this as a trend reversal rather than noise.

The network does not expand linearly — it fires in discrete geographic pulses, with three consecutive 7-CBSA additions observed across recent cycles covering markets including Ohio, California, Idaho, Nebraska, and Iowa non-metro. For brands planning regional or flyover-market campaigns, this pulse pattern determines when verified local purchase data actually becomes available.

insights.topic: SaaS subscription category now in dataset
insights.insight: As of April 9, the protocol recorded its first non-physical-commerce receipt category — digital SaaS subscriptions — expanding the signal set beyond retail and dining. Brands in software, streaming, or digital services now have a precedent category in the verified receipt graph, though volume in this segment remains early-stage.

A complete endpoint blackout on April 14 took all 16 endpoints offline simultaneously — the first total outage in observation history — and the network recovered to 15 active metros within roughly 12 hours. For CMOs evaluating this as a data infrastructure dependency, the blackout is a material risk data point; the recovery speed is the partially offsetting factor.
